subject: computer-science
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: What does the acronym CPU stand for?
questions.explain: The CPU (Central Processing Unit) is the component that carries out the instructions of a program.

questions.q: Which part of the CPU performs arithmetic and logical operations?
questions.explain: The ALU carries out arithmetic calculations and logical comparisons within the CPU.

questions.q: What are the three stages of the machine cycle carried out by the CPU?
questions.explain: The CPU repeatedly fetches an instruction from memory, decodes it and then executes it.

questions.q: Why does increasing the clock speed of a CPU generally improve performance?
options: More fetch-decode-execute cycles can be carried out each second
Each instruction becomes smaller in memory
The amount of RAM available is increased
questions.explain: A higher clock speed means more instruction cycles per second, so more instructions are processed.

questions.q: In which unit is CPU clock speed measured?
questions.explain: Clock speed is measured in hertz, commonly gigahertz (GHz), where 1 GHz is one billion cycles per second.

questions.q: How can adding more cores to a CPU improve performance?
options: Multiple instructions can be processed at the same time
questions.explain: Additional cores allow the CPU to process instructions in parallel, increasing throughput.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of cache memory in a computer?
options: To store frequently used data and instructions close to the CPU for faster access
To provide permanent long-term storage of files
To hold the operating system when the computer is off
To connect peripherals to the motherboard
questions.explain: Cache is fast memory near the CPU that reduces the time needed to fetch commonly used data.

questions.q: Which statement correctly distinguishes RAM from ROM?
options: RAM is volatile and loses its contents when power is off, whereas ROM is non-volatile
ROM is volatile and loses its contents, whereas RAM is non-volatile
Both RAM and ROM lose their contents when powered off
Both RAM and ROM keep their contents when powered off
questions.explain: RAM is volatile working memory, while ROM retains its contents permanently without power.

questions.q: Which of these is an example of system software rather than application software?
questions.explain: The operating system is system software that manages the computer, whereas the others are applications.

questions.q: Which of the following is a key function of an operating system?
options: Compiling source code into machine code
Generating electrical power for the CPU
questions.explain: Managing memory, allocating it to programs, is a core function of the operating system.

questions.q: A program that provides a user interface, manages files and controls peripherals is best described as what?
questions.explain: Providing a user interface and managing files, memory and peripherals are all roles of the operating system.

questions.q: Which task is an example of utility software?
options: Backing up or compressing files on a disk
Editing a photograph for a project
Writing an essay in a document
questions.explain: Utility software performs maintenance tasks such as backup, compression and disk clean-up.

questions.q: What is the job of a translator such as a compiler or interpreter?
options: To convert program code from one form into another so it can be executed
To connect the computer to the internet
To store data permanently on the hard drive
To increase the CPU clock speed
questions.explain: Translators convert source code into machine code (or an intermediate form) that the CPU can run.

questions.q: Which statement best describes the difference between a compiler and an interpreter?
options: A compiler translates the whole program at once, while an interpreter translates and runs it line by line
A compiler runs code line by line, while an interpreter translates it all at once
Both translate the program one line at a time
questions.explain: A compiler produces a complete executable in one go, whereas an interpreter processes each line as the program runs.

questions.q: Why might a programmer choose a high-level language over a low-level language?
options: It is easier for humans to read, write and maintain
It always runs faster than machine code
It removes the need for any translator
It can only be used on one specific processor
questions.explain: High-level languages use human-readable syntax, making programs quicker to write, understand and debug.

questions.q: Which type of translator converts assembly language into machine code?
questions.explain: An assembler translates low-level assembly language into the machine code the CPU executes.

questions.q: How many bits are there in one byte?
questions.explain: One byte is made up of 8 bits; 4 bits form a nibble.

questions.q: How many bits are there in a nibble?
questions.explain: A nibble is half a byte, which is 4 bits.

questions.q: Why is hexadecimal often used by programmers to represent binary values?
options: It is more compact and easier for humans to read than long binary strings
It can store more information than binary
It is the only base a CPU can process
It removes the need to use binary inside the computer
questions.explain: Each hex digit maps to four binary bits, so hex represents binary more concisely and with fewer errors.

questions.q: What is the denary (base 10) value of the binary number 10110101?
What is the denary number 45 written as an 8-bit binary number?
What is the hexadecimal representation of the denary number 47?
questions.explain: 47 = (2 x 16) + 15, and 15 is F in hex, giving 2F.
